hint.layers:
Map layers are displayed on top of each other. Layers that are higher up in the settings are displayed above the other layers in the map.

The layers can be sorted by drag and drop.

The individual map layers can be switched on or off at different zoom levels.

This allows overview and detail maps to be used together.

Map layers that are temporarily not needed can be hidden (eye symbol button).
hint.profiles:
“Profiles” determine how the offline vector maps are displayed by mapsforge.

Built-in themes can be used for the profiles. Or custom themes in xml format.

The profiles can be sorted by drag and drop. The top profile is used as default for all maps that do not have a specific profile assigned.
hint.visibility:
Whether the map layer is switched on or not.

Map layers that are temporarily not required can be switched off.
hint.xyzSource:
The url to the xyz map tile server.

The url must preferably start with https://. Insecure connections with http:// are possible, but are not recommended.

The url must contain the placeholders {X}, {Y} and {Z} (in curly braces).

This map layer requests raster images from an online source. Any request to any server, transferees personal data (your IP address). This is technically necessary.
hint.enabled: Between which zoom levels the map layer is displayed.
hint.zoom: Between which zoom levels the map layer is loaded. If you zoom beyond the maximum zoom level of the map layer, the map will continue to be displayed but will not be updated. This prevents some tile servers from showing placeholders at high zoom levels.
hint.zoomGeneralInfo:
About zoom in general:

At low zoom levels, the zoom is wide and a large area is displayed on the map. At large zoom levels, the map shows a detailed section.

Tip: The dashboard can display the current map zoom level.
hint.mapsforgeFile:
Map files for mapsforge are individual files that contain vector data. The file extension is “.map”.

They must be downloaded manually. Once downloaded, no internet connection is required to use them.

It is recommended to move the downloaded files to one of the Straymap app directories. However, it is also possible to load the map from any publicly accessible directory.
hint.mapsforgeProfile:
Profiles determine how the offline vector maps are displayed by mapsforge.

A profile can be selected for the map layer, which must be configured beforehand. The various mapsforge profiles can generally be managed in the map settings.

If no profile is assigned to the map layer, the first profile is used automatically.
hint.mapsforgeHasBuildings:
This setting determines whether buildings are rendered in 3D. The display of 3D buildings is independent of the render theme.

If this setting is switched off, buildings are rendered in 2D if necessary. Whether and how they are rendered depends solely on the render theme. With xml render themes, this can maybe be configured via the overlay settings, depending on the render theme.
hint.mbTilesFile:
MBtiles map files contain raster images that are stored in an SQLite database. The file extension is “.mbtiles”.

They must be downloaded manually. After downloading, no internet connection is required to use them.

After downloading, the files must be moved to one of the Straymap app directories. It is not possible to load the map from a publicly accessible directory.
hint.demDir:
The DEM directory contains the files for the digital elevation models (DEM). The file extension of the files is “.hgt”.

They must be downloaded manually. After downloading, no internet connection is required to use them.

It is recommended to move the downloaded files to one of the directories of the Straymap app, but it is possible to load the elevation models from any publicly accessible directory.

DEM are usually provided with a resolution of 1 or 3 arc seconds. (One arc second corresponds to approximately 30m at the equator)
hint.demOnly3Sec: Currently, only elevation models with a resolution of 3 arc seconds are supported.
hint.mapsforgeProfileFile:
Themes determine how the offline vector maps are displayed by mapsforge.

Built-in themes can be used. Or custom themes in xml format. The file extension for custom themes is “.xml”.

Custom themes must be downloaded manually and moved to one of the Straymap app directories. It is not possible to load the themes from a publicly accessible directory.
hint.mapsforgeProfileStyle: Themes can contain different styles. These styles are slight variations of the theme.
hint.mapsforgeProfileOverlays:
Overlays determine which elements of the map are visible or not.

Tip: You can switch off the map background. And instead display another map layer (e.g. a satellite map) behind it.
hint.opacity:
The opacity of the map layer.

Value between 0 and 1.

- 0 means the layer is transparent.
- 1 means the layer has full opacity and underlying layers are not visible.
hint.cache: A cache stores map images. So they don't have to get downloaded or generated again.
hint.cacheDir:
The directory where the cache is to be saved.

An internal directory can only be accessed by the app itself. An external directory can also be accessed by other apps, such as File Explorer apps.
hint.cacheSize: The size of the cache in MB.

magnitude.label: Magnitude
magnitude.hint: The magnitude determines the intensity of the shading.

maxSlope.label: Maximum Slope
maxSlope.hint:
The smallest slope that will have the darkest shade.

All larger slopes will have the same shade, the darkest one.

Should be larger than zero.

The default is 80.

[percentage, %]

minSlope.label: Minimum Slope
minSlope.hint:
The largest slope that will have the lightest shade.

All smaller slopes will have the same shade, the lightest one.

Should be in the range of zero and "Maximum Slope".

The default is 0 (zero).

[percentage, %]

asymmetryFactor.label: Asymmetry Factor
asymmetryFactor.hint:
Number between 0 and 1.

When 1 the reference direction (NW by default) slopes will get minimal shading (max asymmetry effect),

when 0 the shading will be symmetrical in all directions (no asymmetry effect).

Any value larger than 0 will make the shading smoothly asymmetrical, with slopes closer to the reference direction less shaded than slopes in the opposite direction as the factor increases.

The default is 0.5
